dtNote: Effective dt per N is gap-seeded: dtEff = min(DT, d_min^2/80). See row.dt for actual dt used (imp514d). Additionally, currentDt is capped to mg^2/12 at each step to prevent late-stage overshoot (imp514f). dysonDerivBackward uses antisymmetry (N*(N-1)/2 pairs, ~2x speedup vs N^2, no Kahan).

subGaps.description: zeros data blocker: FIXED. zeros6 (2M Odlyzko zeros, 36 MB) has been downloaded to scripts/.zeros-cache/zeros6. The harness loads it automatically on every run (no --download flag needed). Covers N up to 2M.

compute feasibility: Float64 RK4 in Node.js handles N up to ~250K-400K (minutes to hours). N=600K-1M requires C/Rust backend (Arb, CAPD, or custom). This script cannot fully close imp-514 for N=1M without native code.

certification: Float64 RK4 gives t_c central value without error bars. Interval arithmetic (interval-dyson-integrator.mjs) is certified but returns budget-exhausted for N>100K. Closing imp-514 with certified bounds at N=1M requires a native Arb/CAPD backend.

step-size overshoot at large N: FIXED (two-stage). Stage 1 (initial overshoot, prior run): dtEff = min(DT, d_min^2/80) is seeded from the initial minimum gap d_min so the first RK4 step cannot overshoot the nearest-pair collapse time T_pair ~ d_min^2/8. Stage 2 (dt-restoration bug, this run): backwardCollisionRK4Float64 now accepts maxDt=DT so the integrator restores currentDt to the original DT (not to dtEff) once mg > 10 * ADAPT_THRESH. Previously, restoration returned to dtEff (e.g. 2.70e-6 at N=150K), keeping the step permanently tiny and covering only stepsEff * dtEff = 300 * 2.70e-6 = 8.1e-4 of the ~0.00668 integration range. With the fix, the integrator recovers to DT=0.0001 after the initial close-pair zone, covering 300 total steps including ~250 at DT=0.0001 => 0.025 time units >> OLS(150K)=0.00668. Wall time is unchanged (~7 hr at N=150K in JS), but the run now returns a meaningful t_c instead of budget-exhausted at t=0.00081.

overshoot detector anchoring bug: FIXED. ADAPT_THRESH was anchored to the gap-seeded initial dt (e.g. 2.70e-6 at N=150K) rather than to maxDt (the restored full DT=0.0001). After currentDt is restored to maxDt, the threshold 3*dtEff << maxDt was too small to trigger adaptive halving for any second close encounter encountered at the restored stride, allowing it to be overshot. Fix: ADAPT_THRESH = 3 * maxDt (and min-step guard uses maxDt/16), so the threshold tracks the actual stride in use.

gap-safe step cap: FIXED. The adaptive-halving formula used mg/4 as the reduced step, which is O(mg) not O(mg^2). After restoration to maxDt, if the gap has decayed to g << sqrt(8*maxDt), then maxDt >> t_c_pair = g^2/8 and the next full step overshoots. Example: N=10K, initial gap 0.0377, after step 0 gap ~ 0.025, t_c_pair ~ 7.8e-5 << DT=1e-4 so step 1 overshoots. Fix: after the adaptive/restore block, cap currentDt to mg^2/12 (2/3 of t_c_pair). With this cap, gap^2 shrinks by factor 1/3 per step, reaching machine-epsilon in ~log3(gap0/eps) ≈ 30-40 steps << stepsEff, and the post-step check detects the collision accurately.

collision-threshold bug: FIXED. COLLISION_THRESHOLD was 0, meaning the gap had to literally cross zero to trigger the nonpositive-gap check. But the mg^2/12 cap (imp514f) causes the minimum gap to converge geometrically toward 0 (ratio ~1/sqrt(3) per step) without ever reaching 0 in float64 arithmetic. Result: 300 steps exhausted, t_c = 0.000178 (budget-exhausted) instead of gap-nonpositive. Fix: COLLISION_THRESHOLD = 1e-10. The geometric tail terminates in ~30 additional steps, reporting the correct t_c. Methodology note: Odlyzko zeros have small initial minimum gaps (~0.037 at N=10K, ~0.0147 at N=150K), so the measured t_c ~ g_min^2/8 is much smaller than the OLS-extrapolated value (PATH_C_FIT_POINTS used R-S scan zeros with larger forced minimum spacing). Both are valid measurements of different initial conditions; the discrepancy is not a bug.

usageNote: Import these rows into dyson-ladder-measured.js to replace PROJECTED_ROWS at matching N. Only rows with source="measured-float64-rk4" and reason="gap-nonpositive" carry a meaningful collision time. Budget-exhausted rows report t_c as a lower bound.
